name: Vansen SyncPulse Haptic Interface Glove
description:
Slim-profile gloves in charcoal stretch-neoprene with embedded haptic actuator nodes at each fingertip and across the palm grid. Thin silver conductive traces are visible through the semi-translucent neoprene like circuit diagrams. Fingertips of the index and middle fingers on both hands are open-cut with conductive trim rings for direct augment-digit contact.

Designed to bridge organic and chrome hands simultaneously — the palm grid reads BCI signals and translates them into precise haptic feedback for remote manipulation, surgical assist, or AR interface use. Ships with a calibration dongle that clips to the wrist strap.
functionality: Haptic actuators provide tactile feedback in AR/VR environments and for remote robotic manipulation. Open-cut conductive fingertips allow direct chrome-digit BCI handshake. Palm grid reads passive BCI output. Calibration dongle syncs to most commercial neural port standards.
what_it_says: Precision work at the boundary of organic and machine — someone who earns through interface mastery.
story_hooks: A counterfeit batch of SyncPulse gloves has been traced to a Shelf workshop — they work fine but log all haptic input to an unknown server.
A remote surgeon relies on these gloves for operations across the city; when they malfunction mid-procedure, someone has to make a choice.
The calibration dongle format is compatible with a decommissioned military drone protocol — someone's been using consumer gloves to fly something they shouldn't.
